{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "partial",
    "answerable": [
      "Simulate long-term mean annual drainage flux at the bottom of the ELM soil column (a model-based proxy for potential recharge) across representative Naches locations",
      "Bound recharge sensitivity to soil texture and meteorological forcing over 1980-2018",
      "Provide climatological-mean 'quasi-steady-state' recharge estimates by cycling forcing to equilibrium"
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "The 'true' recharge — no direct recharge observations exist for the Naches to validate against (only WTD priors and USGS well levels)",
      "True steady-state deep-water-table recharge — ELM's fixed/finite soil column does not resolve a deep regional water table; that requires coupling to a groundwater model (PFLOTRAN) with calibrated hydraulic properties",
      "Spatially continuous basin-wide recharge fields — single-column configuration yields point estimates, not a distributed basin flux"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 4,
  "n_justification": "The Naches spans ~1600 m of relief (352-1977 m) with strong orographic precipitation and snowpack gradients plus contrasting soils. Four columns span a low-valley, mid-elevation, high-elevation snow-dominated, and a coarse-soil comparison site to bracket the recharge range and isolate the two candidate drivers (soil vs forcing) without over-fitting an under-observed target.",
  "columns": [
    {

      "lat": 46.73,

    },
    {

      "lat": 46.68,
      "lon": -120.6,
      "soil_texture": "loamy sand"
    }
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1980",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2018",
    "STOP_N": "39",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "1980-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "QDRAI",
      "QDRAI_PERCH",
      "QRECHARGE",
      "QOVER",
      "QRUNOFF",
      "QINFL",
      "SOILLIQ",
      "SOILICE",
      "H2OSOI",
      "ZWT",

      "SNOWDP",
      "H2OSNO",
      "QVEGT",
      "QSOIL",
      "EFLX_LH_TOT",
      "TSOI"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": [
    "ELM single-column (PTS_MODE) simulations with spin-up to hydrologic equilibrium",
    "Site-specific meteorological forcing (1980-2018) downscaled for orographic gradient",
    "Soil texture / hydraulic parameter specification per column (surface dataset override)",
    "PFLOTRAN coupling (or offline groundwater model) to translate soil-column drainage into deep-water-table recharge if a true deep-WT flux is required",
    "USGS well WTD and Fan 2013 prior for evaluating simulated ZWT plausibility"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "'Recharge' is approximated by ELM bottom-of-column drainage QDRAI/QRECHARGE; this is a potential recharge proxy, not a validated deep-WT flux",
    "'Steady state' is interpreted as the multi-decadal climatological mean after an accelerated-decomposition + hydrologic spin-up (multiple cycles of 1980-2018 forcing) to remove initialization transients",
    "The deep regional water table lies below the ELM soil column; vadose-zone lag and deep percolation losses are not resolved without a groundwater model",
    "No recharge observations exist, so results are presented as model-based estimates with driver-sensitivity ranges rather than a single 'true' value",
    "Forcing is assumed representative at each point; sub-grid orographic and lateral flow processes are neglected in single-column mode"
  ]
}

parsed.n_justification: The Naches spans ~1600 m of relief (352-1977 m) with strong orographic precipitation and snowpack gradients plus contrasting soils. Four columns span a low-valley, mid-elevation, high-elevation snow-dominated, and a coarse-soil comparison site to bracket the recharge range and isolate the two candidate drivers (soil vs forcing) without over-fitting an under-observed target.
requires_capabilities: ELM single-column (PTS_MODE) simulations with spin-up to hydrologic equilibrium
Site-specific meteorological forcing (1980-2018) downscaled for orographic gradient
Soil texture / hydraulic parameter specification per column (surface dataset override)
PFLOTRAN coupling (or offline groundwater model) to translate soil-column drainage into deep-water-table recharge if a true deep-WT flux is required
USGS well WTD and Fan 2013 prior for evaluating simulated ZWT plausibility
assumptions: 'Recharge' is approximated by ELM bottom-of-column drainage QDRAI/QRECHARGE; this is a potential recharge proxy, not a validated deep-WT flux

'Steady state' is interpreted as the multi-decadal climatological mean after an accelerated-decomposition + hydrologic spin-up (multiple cycles of 1980-2018 forcing) to remove initialization transients
The deep regional water table lies below the ELM soil column; vadose-zone lag and deep percolation losses are not resolved without a groundwater model
No recharge observations exist, so results are presented as model-based estimates with driver-sensitivity ranges rather than a single 'true' value
Forcing is assumed representative at each point; sub-grid orographic and lateral flow processes are neglected in single-column mode
